verdict.rationale: CloudConvert is an API service, so machine-readable success and failure signaling is a fair axis. The evidence shows only a glancing piece of it: a documented HTTP 429 status with a Retry-After header for rate limits, plus real-time task updates over the Socket API. Neither shows a general scheme for telling job or task success from failure. Missing for 10: documented status/error codes for job and task failures, structured task status fields (e.g. finished/error), error logs or messages per task, any CLI exit-code behavior, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, the tool returns meaningful exit codes and logs, so a pipeline can tell success from failure without parsing prose

citations.quote: If the limit is reached, a 429 error is returned, and there is a Retry-After header with the time in seconds to wait before the next request.
Socket API: Real-time task updates using Socket.io.
